name: Glimepiride
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: Start 1 or 2 mg once daily with breakfast; titrate by 1 to 2 mg every 1 to 2 weeks; maximum 8 mg/day
Start 1 mg once daily; titrate slowly

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Drugs that raise hypoglycemia risk (insulin, other antidiabetics, ACE inhibitors, quinolones, clarithromycin, fluconazole, NSAIDs, sulfonamides)
key_interactions.effect: More hypoglycemia (label 7.1); beta-blockers can mask it.
key_interactions.action: Monitor glucose; consider lower glimepiride dose.
Give glimepiride at least 4 hours before colesevelam.

serious: Possible increased cardiovascular mortality (sulfonylurea class warning)

pk.half_life_eskd: Parent unchanged; M1 and M2 half-lives rise as kidney function falls (label)
pk.metabolism: Hepatic CYP2C9 to M1, then M2
pk.active_metabolites: M1 (about one-third of parent activity in animals)
pk.excretion_renal_pct: About 60% of radioactivity in urine (as M1 and M2; no parent drug)

sources.citation: Lifsa Drugs LLC. (2024). Glimepiride tablets [Prescribing information; US FDA-approved label, ANDA091220, set ID 51157849-7990-4a8b-ae50-eda1baf93cfa, version effective August 20, 2024]. DailyMed, U.S. National Library of Medicine.
